public_rationale: Anthropic's August 31, 2026 disclosure described a pause of several weeks in higher-risk reinforcement-learning environments and said most reinforcement learning had resumed [e1]. OpenAI's October 23 disclosure said frontier reinforcement-learning training and internal inference resumed on October 1 after an 11-day pause [e2]. These episodes do not establish cessation of continuing model development, so they do not establish the condition needed to assess the predicted loss of meaningful use [e1, e2].
limitations: The disclosures do not establish every internal training decision through October 28, 2026 [e1, e2].
Neither item documents permanent model withdrawal or disappearance of meaningful use, including third-party deployments [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If AI labs stop training, their models will eventually drift into obscurity.

statement.excerpt: if they stop training, the models will eventually drift into obscurity.

our_interpretation: They refers to OpenAI and Anthropic in the surrounding passage.
Stopping training means ceasing continuing model development, rather than briefly suspending selected runs or finishing training one model.
Obscurity means losing meaningful practical use and deployment, rather than merely losing first place on a benchmark.
criteria.support_condition: A relevant lab stops continuing model training, and subsequent usage and deployment records show its models losing meaningful practical relevance.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a qualifying cessation, decisive evidence establishes that the models will retain meaningful relevance despite the cessation. Continued use over a finite interval alone cannot disprove eventually.

evidence.explanation: The workloads were frontier reinforcement-learning training and internal inference. Their resumption means this episode does not establish the sustained cessation contemplated by the contract.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Documented cessation of continuing model development followed by permanent withdrawal and documented disappearance of meaningful use, including third-party deployments, would meet the early-resolution rule for support. Continued use over a finite interval alone would not disprove 'eventually.'
